Serial constraints cleared: all **19** open PRs' changed-file lists fetched **paged to exhaustion** at 2026-09-08T14:1xZ and filtered for `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` — **zero hits**; control, 19 of 19 returned a non-empty list.

## ⛔ #16361 is held behind this card by this seat

The card says it in terms: #16361 is the **same gate, same file, opposite direction** (a false red from predicate scope), ⛔ neither subsumes the other, and they "collide on `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` ⇒ schedule in one window". #16361 stays `pm:queue` until this PR is MERGED or closed. ⇒ ⛔ Do not fix #16361's predicate-scope defect here, however tempting it is with the file open. If your reading shows the two fixes are genuinely one edit, ⛔ do not merge them on your own judgement — say so in the report and this seat will answer fold-or-serial.

## ⭐ Re-drive the measurements first — the card orders it and it is cheap

The card's **Boundaries** block is explicit: every reading in it is second-hand (the #15963 implementer's, relayed through #16361's filer) and ⛔ **not re-driven by triage**. Also ⚠️ the run ids and timestamps are from 2026-09-06 and the workflow may have moved.

1. **Re-derive the trigger list from `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml` on your worktree's base**, not from the card. (For your orientation, this seat read `:5` as `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled]` at 14:1xZ — ⛔ treat that as a hint to check, not as a reading you may inherit.)
2. **Re-run defect A's three-row table** — it is one script invocation per row against an `--event` payload, and it *is* the whole of defect A. Carry a **firing control and a nonsense control**; a table of three rows with no control proves nothing.
3. Only then choose a fix.

## What "fixed" has to mean here

⭐ The card's sharpest point is the one to build against: **the merge queue and the required-check set read the check-run conclusion, not the step log.** A gate that prints `LEVEL AXIS: NOT MEASURED` into a log nobody with merge authority reads, and concludes `success`, is this repo's own stated failure class — *a reading that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed* — turned on its own CI.

⇒ Whatever you choose, the distinction must reach the layer that gates a merge. If you take the `output`/`summary` route rather than the conclusion route, you owe an argument for why that surface is actually read by merge authority, and ⛔ "a careful reviewer could see it" is not that argument.

⛔ **No tolerance, no allowlist, no comment-only heuristic** — carried from #16361's body, and the card restates it. ⛔ Do not weaken the gate to make a case go green.

⚠️ If you take the `edited` trigger for defect B, the card's own warning is an acceptance obligation: it fires on **every** body edit including title/description churn ⇒ measure and state the added run volume. If you take the cheaper route (the `Clause-②:` line must be present from the PR's first push), then the thing you are changing is partly **os-dev's own contract**, which lives in `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` — ⛔ that path is a **governed surface** this seat cannot land. Stop and report rather than editing it; the gate half may still be landable on its own.

**LANDED** — PR #16897 merged 2026-09-08T15:55:35Z (merge queue; `added_to_merge_queue` 15:29:42Z, `merged` 15:55:35Z, read from the timeline).

Verified on a re-fetched `origin/main`, not on the report:

| probe | want | got |
|---|---|---|
| `pr-automation.yml`: `types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled, edited]` | 1 | **1** |
| `github.event.action != 'edited'` exclusions (Check PR Size + Auto Label) | 2 | **2** |
| `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` carries `not-measured-material` | >0 | 6 |
| … `not-measured-moot` | >0 | 4 |
| … `no-pull-request` | >0 | 6 |
| nonsense control | 0 | 0 |

⭐ The **2** is the load-bearing number, not the trigger line: `edited` is subscribed once and excluded from the two jobs whose input is the diff, so the ~+15 % event volume buys **one** job rather than three. A probe that only found `edited` in the `types:` list would have passed on a change that tripled the cost.

## Both defects, and why they were one card

**A** — `NOT MEASURED` and `PASSED` shared exit 0, so the check-run conclusion could not tell "judged and passed" from "had nothing to judge". The verdict machine now splits by **materiality**: `not-measured-moot` (no changeset grades `patch` a package the diff grew ⇒ `yes` and `no` reach the same answer) stays exit 0 **and says why it is green**; `not-measured-material` (a `patch` sits on a package the diff grew ⇒ the declaration decides) exits 1, naming the changeset, the package and both declarations.

**B** — the gate never re-read a `Clause-②:` line added after the last push. ⭐ And B is not a convenience next to A: the remedy for A's new refusal **is a PR-body edit**, and a `pull_request` payload is a snapshot that `rerun_failed_jobs` replays — so without `edited` the new red could not be cleared without pushing a commit. A is unshippable without B. That wiring is pinned in the self-test, not argued in prose.

## ⭐ Two inherited readings that did not survive re-driving — both re-verified by this seat

1. **The card (and #16361's comment `5560230929`) say the Check Changeset job "skips label events". It does not.** On the base, only two jobs carry an action exclusion — `:99` Check PR Size and `:164` Auto Label. `changeset-check`'s own `if:` has none.
2. **`Check Changeset` is not in the required-check set at all.** Read live from ruleset `12119582`: 7 required contexts, and this is not one of them. ⇒ the card's merge-authority sentence was wider than the fact — **and that strengthens the route taken**: the conclusion is not merely a layer merge authority reads, it is the **only** authority this gate has, and the same one its existing "you forgot a changeset" verdict already rides. The `output`/`summary` alternative was measured and is unavailable: a real run's check-run `output.title` is `null` and its summary empty, because an Actions job publishes no check-run output of its own.

## The specimen, re-verified independently

**PR #16775**, merged today 07:19:53Z: `Clause-②: no` written **inside a sentence**, line-start matches for `^Clause-②:` = **0**; carries `.changeset/rest-server-config-embedder-only-reachability.md` grading `"@objectstack/spec": patch`, and moves one `packages/spec/src/**` file. ⇒ a `patch` on a package it grew, with the declaration unreadable, merged under a green check. This card, live. ⛔ Nothing is owed retroactively — all 69 packages sit in one `fixed` group and the released bump is set by the highest pending changeset either way.

⛔ **Not claimed by this seat**: the 45-merge blast-radius sweep (exactly one row flips 0 → 1). This container has no `node_modules`, so the script refuses with a prerequisite error rather than running — a failed read, not a reading. I verified the one row the sweep turns on; the other 30 are the implementer's.

## Downstream

**#16361 is UNBLOCKED** — same two files, opposite direction. ⛔ Still not a fold: this changed the verdict/exit machine and the trigger list; #16361 is about which packages the `yes` predicate applies to. It wants a **rebase** onto this, not a merge with it.

**Routed to the maintainer, not answered here**: should `Check Changeset` be enrolled as a required context? It is advisory today, so every verdict it makes — the new refusal included — is a red X that blocks nothing mechanically. ⛔ Out of this card's reach: enrolment is a ruleset edit no PR can make, and it would also oblige the workflow to grow a `merge_group:` trigger and a `REQUIRED_CONTEXTS` entry. Recommendation: leave advisory for now, decide deliberately rather than by silence.

## ⭐ The end-to-end verification this card owed — taken live, 34 minutes after the fix merged, on an unrelated PR

I did not construct this. **PR #16916** (an unrelated `packages/lint` card, opened after this landed) walked straight into the exact failure this card describes, and the fix caught it and cleared it — both halves, in sequence, on one head.

### The sequence, all on head `ea8564d001`, nothing pushed between

| time | event | `Check Changeset` |
|---|---|---|
| 16:24:43Z | first run (`synchronize`) | **failure** — run `102144677169` |
| ~16:29:02Z | I edited the PR **body** to add a line-start `Clause-②: no` | — |
| **16:29:10Z** | the `edited` trigger fired — **8 seconds later**, no push, no commit, no re-run request | second run `102146214309` starts |
| 16:29:5xZ | | **success** |

**Two runs of the same check on the same commit SHA, and the second one exists only because the body changed.**

### Defect A, caught in the wild

PR #16916 carries `"@objectstack/lint": patch` and moves `packages/lint/src/**` — a `patch` on a package the diff grew — with no readable declaration in its body. That is precisely `not-measured-material`. ⭐ **Before this card, that PR would have gone green**: the old single `NOT MEASURED` verdict exited 0, and the level ruling would simply never have been applied to it. Instead the gate refused, and its message named the changeset, the package and both declarations.

⭐ And the refusal text carries its own remedy, correctly:

> ⛔ The remedy is the declaration, never the deletion: dropping the changeset, or regrading the package to dodge this message, changes what ships in order to quiet a gate. And the line is read from the body on the next `edited` event (pr-automation.yml subscribes to it), so this red clears with no push and no re-run.

### Defect B, proved by the clock

That last sentence is a promise the gate could not have kept 34 minutes earlier. The 16:29:10Z run **is** the proof: the payload for the 16:24:43Z run was a frozen snapshot that no `rerun_failed_jobs` could refresh, and without the `edited` subscription the only way to clear that red would have been to push a commit — the "manufacture a `synchronize`" manoeuvre PR #16342 had to perform by hand.

⇒ **A is unshippable without B** was the argument in this PR's body. It is now a measurement rather than an argument.

### What this does not show

⛔ It does not exercise `not-measured-moot`, `no-pull-request`, or the malformed-declaration path — those remain covered by the self-test only, as far as this seat has driven them. And ⛔ the 45-merge blast-radius sweep is still the implementer's reading, not mine; this container cannot run the script.
